name: Mumbai
tagline: India's biggest, fastest and most cosmopolitan city: Victorian Gothic railway stations, Art Deco seafront blocks, Bollywood dreams and the country's best street food.
highlight: A stroll along Marine Drive at dusk, as the lights come on along the Queen's Necklace.
shortDescription: The financial and film capital of India, with the Gateway of India, the UNESCO-listed Victorian and Art Deco ensembles, Elephanta Caves, street food and a vibrant arts scene.
metaDescription: A Mumbai travel guide: the Gateway of India, Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, Marine Drive, Elephanta Caves, Colaba, Dhobi Ghat, street food, local trains, when to go and a three-day plan.
nearestAirport: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International (BOM), about 45 minutes to 1 hour
knownFor: The Gateway of India, Art Deco and Victorian buildings, Bollywood, street food
goodFor: Architecture, food, urban energy, nightlife, a gateway to Goa

intro: Mumbai, formerly Bombay, is India's largest city and the engine of its economy, with more than 12 million people in the city itself and about 20 million in the wider metropolitan area. It grew from seven islands, ceded by the Portuguese to the British in 1661 as part of a royal dowry, into one of the great ports of the British Empire, and it kept growing after independence as a centre of finance, industry and film.

The colonial legacy is unusually visible. South Mumbai has the largest collection of Victorian Gothic buildings in the world outside Britain, including the Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, and along Marine Drive and Oval Maidan a large group of 1930s Art Deco apartments and cinemas. UNESCO listed the Victorian and Art Deco ensemble in 2018.

Beyond the architecture, Mumbai is a city of contrasts, of gleaming towers and huge slums, of Bollywood studios and street-side tea stalls, of daily commuters packed into local trains and of a food culture that ranges from vada pav at street corners to fine dining. It is a good place to see modern India, and its energy is infectious.

whyVisit.intro: Mumbai is a different India from the north, faster, more modern and more mixed.

points.title: Colonial and Art Deco architecture
points.text: Two UNESCO listings cover the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco buildings of the south.

points.title: Street food
points.text: Vada pav, pav bhaji, bhel puri, kebabs and Irani café chai, among the best snacks in India.

points.title: Bollywood and culture
points.text: Film studios, theatres, art galleries and the country's biggest music scene.

points.title: Elephanta Caves
points.text: A short ferry ride to rock-cut temples dedicated to Shiva.

points.title: The sea
points.text: Marine Drive, Chowpatty and the promenades along the Arabian Sea.

attractionsIntro: Most sights are in South Mumbai, and can be visited on foot and by short taxi rides.

attractions.name: The Gateway of India
attractions.text: A basalt arch on the waterfront, built in 1924 to commemorate the visit of King George V and Queen Mary in 1911, and the point from which the last British troops left India in 1948. Ferries to Elephanta leave from here.
attractions.tip: Go early or late, to avoid the crowds and heat.

attractions.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus

image.alt: The Victorian Gothic façade of Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus railway station in Mumbai

attractions.text: The great railway station, completed in 1887 as Victoria Terminus, is a fantasy of domes, turrets and carved stone in Victorian Gothic and Indian styles. It is still a working station used by millions.
attractions.tip: Look at the exterior from the road, and walk in to see the concourse.

attractions.name: Marine Drive

image.alt: The curving Marine Drive promenade beside the Arabian Sea in Mumbai

attractions.text: A curving promenade of about 3.5 km along Back Bay, lined with Art Deco buildings, and known as the Queen's Necklace for its lights at night. A favourite evening walk.

attractions.name: Elephanta Caves

image.alt: Rock-cut columns inside the Elephanta Caves near Mumbai

attractions.text: A UNESCO-listed cave temple complex on an island in the harbour, carved in the 5th to 8th centuries, with a huge sculpture of the three-faced Shiva. A ferry from the Gateway of India takes about an hour.
attractions.tip: Closed on Mondays, and take the earliest ferry.

attractions.name: Colaba and Kala Ghoda
attractions.text: The area around the Gateway has a mix of cafés, bookshops, art galleries and the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalya museum, in an Indo-Saracenic building.
attractions.tip: Walk the Kala Ghoda art district.

attractions.name: Dhobi Ghat and Haji Ali
attractions.text: An open-air laundry where clothes are washed by hand, seen from a bridge, and the Haji Ali Dargah, a mosque and tomb on a causeway in the sea.
attractions.tip: Visit Haji Ali at low tide when the causeway is open.

thingsToDoIntro: Mumbai rewards a mix of walking, eating and riding its transport.

thingsToDo.title: Take a local train
thingsToDo.text: The suburban rail system carries about 7 million passengers a day, and a short ride is an experience in itself.
thingsToDo.tip: Avoid rush hours, and use the first-class or women's carriage if you prefer.

thingsToDo.title: Eat street food
thingsToDo.text: Sample vada pav, pav bhaji, bhel puri and kulfi at Chowpatty, Juhu and around the stations.

thingsToDo.title: Visit an Irani café
thingsToDo.text: Old Parsi-Irani cafés serve bun maska, chai and keema pav in period interiors.
thingsToDo.tip: Try Kyani & Co. or other established cafés.

thingsToDo.title: See the art scene
thingsToDo.text: Galleries in Kala Ghoda and the museum of modern art give a taste of India's contemporary art.
thingsToDo.tip: Visit during the Kala Ghoda Arts Festival.

thingsToDo.title: Walk through Bandra
thingsToDo.text: The suburb has street art, cafés and shops, and is popular for evenings.

thingsToDo.title: Watch a cricket match on the maidans
thingsToDo.text: Cricket games take place on open grounds across the city on weekends.

foodIntro: Mumbai's food is defined by its street snacks, its seafood and its mixed communities.

foods.name: Vada pav
foods.text: A spiced potato fritter in a soft bun with chutneys, and the city's iconic snack.

foods.name: Pav bhaji
foods.text: A buttery vegetable mash with toasted rolls.

foods.name: Bhel puri
foods.text: Puffed rice tossed with chutneys, onion and crisp noodles.

foods.name: Bombay duck and seafood
foods.text: Fresh fish and prawns cooked in Koli and Goan styles. Bombay duck is a dried fish, not a bird.
foods.whereToTry: Seafood restaurants in Colaba and Bandra.

foods.name: Irani café classics
foods.text: Bun maska, keema pav and Irani chai in old cafés.

foods.name: Kulfi and falooda
foods.text: Rich frozen dessert and rose-flavoured milk drinks.

accommodation.intro: South Mumbai is convenient for sightseeing, and Bandra and Juhu are better for nightlife.

areas.name: Colaba and Fort
areas.text: Hotels near the Gateway of India, cafés and museums.

areas.name: Bandra and Juhu
areas.text: A more residential area, near the airport.

gettingThere.intro: Mumbai is the busiest air hub in western India.

options.text: Direct flights from Europe, the Middle East, Asia and other Indian cities.
options.detail: Traffic to the city can take an hour or more.

options.text: Long-distance trains from Delhi (about 16 hours on the Rajdhani, less on Vande Bharat), Goa and Pune.
About 1 hour by air, or 8 to 12 hours by train or road.

gettingAround.intro: Distances are long and traffic is heavy, so plan by area.

options.text: Black-and-yellow taxis use meters, and apps such as Uber and Ola work.
options.detail: Insist on the meter or use apps.

options.text: The Western, Central and Harbour lines cover the suburbs, and metro lines are growing.
South Mumbai's colonial core can be explored on foot.

bestTime.headline: November–February
bestTime.summary: Mumbai is hot and humid for most of the year, with a heavy monsoon from June to September.

seasons.text: Heavy rain, flooding at times, and green landscapes. Ganesh Chaturthi in August or September is a big festival.
Warm and humid, with clearing skies.

bestTime.avoid: Peak monsoon weeks in July and August, when flooding can disrupt travel.

itinerary.title: Three days in Mumbai
itinerary.intro: Colonial Mumbai first, then Elephanta and the neighbourhoods.

days.title: Colonial South Mumbai
days.morning: The Gateway of India and Colaba.
days.afternoon: The museum and Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus.

tipsIntro: Mumbai is fast, and a few tips help.
tips: Use the black-and-yellow taxis with meters, or ride-hailing apps.
Avoid travel in rush hours (about 8–11am and 5–9pm).
Take the first ferry to Elephanta.
Carry small notes for taxis and tips.
Carry a rain jacket during the monsoon.
Eat at busy places, and avoid raw salads.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Mumbai?
faq.a: Two or three days. One day covers the Gateway of India and the colonial core.
Generally, yes, with the usual big-city precautions. Watch for pickpockets in crowds.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit?

faq.a: Yes, particularly for food, architecture and a modern side of India.
Studio tours are available, though filming is often closed to the public.

faq.q: How do I get to Elephanta Caves?
faq.a: By ferry from the Gateway of India, about an hour each way. The caves are closed on Mondays.
